title: 7.11 Luis is the tallest
unit_title: Everyday needs, plans and free time
unit_outcome: Say what hurts and why someone feels a certain way, describe what people are wearing and the weather as it happens, tell someone to put on or take off clothes, talk about what people like doing, invite and answer, ask someone to repeat or explain, talk about being sick, the months and seasons, compare with the biggest and the tallest, and say what people and animals can do and are good at.
goal: Compare three people or things with the + -est (Luis is the tallest. / The white flower is the smallest.) and ask Which … is the biggest?.
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 7.11 Outdoors: A1 names the things outdoors (This is a tree. This is a flower.); A1+ 7.11 compares three of them. The one new grammar relationship is the + adjective + -est for the top of three (Luis is the tallest. / The yellow flower is the biggest.), set against A1+ 2.11's -er than for two (Ana is taller than Sofia.); big doubles its g (bigger, biggest). Three photos line up three of a kind: Sofia, Ana and Luis by height, three flowers by size and three trees by height, so A1 7.11's flower and tree come back in every stage; A1+ 2.10's The yellow one. answers Which …?.
prerequisite: A1 7.11 tree and flower; A1+ 2.10 Which one? The red one.; A1+ 2.11 -er than; A1 2.11 big and small; A1 2.7 colors.
speaking_outcome: Say the -est ending clearly (TALL-ist, BIG-ist, SMALL-ist) and stress the adjective. Do not require native-like speed.
